newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Fidel Ramos said Executive Secretary Ruben Torres was speaking for himself and not for the ruling party Lakas when he said that the party's leaders are preparing the groundwork for an official position in support of extending term limits for elected officials. (TODAY)

- President Fidel Ramos will call a meeting of all members of Lakas to decide once and for all the party's stand on Constitutional amendments, House Speaker Jose de Venecia said. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Vice President Joseph Estrada threatened to part ways with President Fidel Ramos and lead a nationwide protest action should Malacanang pursue its plan to have the 1987 Constitution amended. (THE MANILA TIMES)
- The Philippine government has assured the International Monetary Fund it would be able to maintain its budget surplus and reduce its debt over the next few years. (TODAY)
- UEM-Mara Philippines Corp, a unit of Renong Berhad of Malaysia, is seeking government incentives for the construction of a 7.28-billion peso Manila-Cavite toll expressway. ( BUSINESS DAILY)
